metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Macao (China)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports international comparisons for Macao (China) using PISA 2022 assessment results. The factsheet does not describe the microdata extraction or whether complex survey sampling weights (and replicate weights) were applied in the computations shown; therefore the weighting strategy is not explicitly auditable from the provided text. For PISA analyses, analysts should use the official PISA sampling weights and replicate weights (when available) to account for the stratified, clustered sampling design and to produce correct standard errors. The factsheet also reports creative thinking proficiency on a 60-point scale, which in PISA is typically derived from the PISA scaling model and plausible values; however, the PV computation/combining approach is not documented in this factsheet excerpt.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The document is a descriptive factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking results (means, score differences, proficiency levels, and correlations) rather than reporting an empirical student-level predictive model with an explicit PV estimation/combining procedure. Because no analysis pipeline is described here (no model training, no PV estimation method, and no missing-data procedure), the plausible-values and missing-data handling details are not available from the provided text. This is a reporting gap for methodological transparency at the level of PV combining and missing-data treatment.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports that in Macao (China), 4,384 students in 46 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 4,400 15-year-olds (about 98% of the total 15-year-old population). No further analytic exclusions (e.g., item nonresponse thresholds, missing background questionnaire rules, or creative-thinking task completion filters) are described in the provided excerpt.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD factsheet summarizes PISA 2022 Creative Thinking results for 15-year-old students in Macao (China). The creative thinking assessment contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving). Macao (China) has a mean creative thinking score of 32/60, which is significantly below the OECD average (33). The factsheet also reports proficiency distribution (77% at least Level 3; 22% at Level 5 or 6) and relative performance patterns: students are relatively stronger in evaluating and improving ideas and relatively weaker in generating diverse ideas. It further documents within-Macao gaps by socioeconomic status (7.1 score points between top and bottom quartiles) and gender (girls +3.8 points), and provides descriptive associations with mathematics and reading performance (correlations of 0.66 and 0.64, respectively).
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet that reports descriptive statistics and benchmark comparisons rather than an original empirical ML/predictive analysis. Consequently, there is no student-level modeling target, no ML algorithm evaluation, and no reported predictive performance metrics to populate main_findings or ml_techniques. The extraction therefore focuses on assessment design and reported outcome summaries, while leaving ML-specific fields empty by design.
